46138: Evangelical commentators (for example Craig Keener and D. A. Carson) agree there is no contradiction: visible good works are right when they point to God, and wrong when they serve self. The evangelistic instinct to let works be seen is biblical, if the motive is God's glory.
46139: This keeps gifts from becoming either hidden out of false modesty or displayed out of pride.
46141: Revivalist tradition; Kevin DeYoung and Greg Gilbert; John Piper; many mission agencies
46142: Because people face eternal destinies, proclaiming Christ has a unique urgency. The church's distinct mission is to make disciples. Christians should do good work, but the church must not let other good things crowd out evangelism.
46143: Takes eternity and the Great Commission seriously; guards against the loss of evangelism seen in some mainline churches; has inspired great sacrifice and missionary love.
46144: At popular level it can create a sacred/secular split, art as propaganda and people as projects. Critics say it can shrink the Bible's story to rescue from the world rather than renewal of it.

46174: List what you do well, what you love doing, and what others regularly ask you to help with. Include both 'church' gifts and work, craft and home skills.
46175: Ask three people who know you well (one from church, one from work or school, one from family) what they see as your gifts. Write down their answers without arguing.
46176: Compare the lists. Where do they agree? Where do others see something you do not?
46177: For each gift, write one way it builds up the church and one way it serves people outside the church.
46178: Pray, thanking God by name for each gift (1 Cor 4:7).
46179: The Bezalel reading: a small group study
46180: Read Exod 31:1-11, Exod 35:30-36:7 and Exod 39:42-43 aloud.
46181: Note every phrase about skill, wisdom, the Spirit, willing hearts and teaching.
46182: Discuss: Why might God give the first 'filling with the Spirit' to an artist? What does it say about your own work?
46183: Read Exod 31:12-17. Discuss why the Sabbath command comes right after the call to build.
46184: Each person names one piece of work they will do this week 'with skill, for glory and for beauty'.
46186: Write the names of five people you work or study with.
46187: Pray for each by name every day for a month, for their good and not only their conversion.
46188: Ask: how can my work serve them better this week? Do one concrete thing.
46189: Notice natural openings to speak about your hope, and take them gently (1 Pet 3:15). Do not force any.
46190: At the end of the month, reflect: did I treat them as neighbours or as targets?
46192: Choose a day or half-day this week to stop productive work.
46193: Do something creative or beautiful with no goal: walk, draw, cook, play music, read poetry.
46194: Say a blessing or prayer of thanks over ordinary things: food, light, people.
46195: Afterwards, write down how it felt to be loved without producing anything.
46196: Read Exod 20:8-11 and Deut 5:12-15 and discuss what freedom the Sabbath gives.
46197: Craft and message: an honest review
46198: Pick one piece of 'Christian' art, music or media and one piece of art by a Christian that does not mention faith directly.
46199: Ask of each: Is it true? Is it well made? Is it beautiful? Does it love its audience?
46200: Discuss Schaeffer's claim that art does not need to justify itself as evangelism, and DeYoung and Gilbert's concern that the church not forget to proclaim.
46201: If you make things, choose one thing to improve in your craft this month.
